input: Pick a godparent for the new baby

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Are they choosing one godparent or a godmother AND godfather? This changes how many people and decisions are involved.
Do they already have specific candidates in mind, or do they need help thinking through who to consider from scratch?
Is this tied to a religious ceremony (baptism, christening) or is it a secular/honorary role? This heavily shapes the criteria for choosing.
Are there family expectations, cultural traditions, or obligations (e.g., a relative must be chosen) that limit the options?
What qualities matter most to the user — e.g., close friendship, same faith, financial stability, geographic closeness — defines who the right person is.
What is the immediate next step — brainstorming names, comparing candidates, scripting how to ask the chosen person, or something else?
Is there any sensitivity around the choice, such as not wanting to offend family members who are not chosen, that should shape how the plan is handled?

gold.taskTitle: Choose a godparent for the new baby
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to select and confirm a godparent (or godparents) for their newborn, which involves identifying candidates, making a decision, and likely asking the chosen person.

questions.title: How many godparents are you choosing — one or two?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is selecting a single godparent or both a godmother and a godfather, as this changes the full scope of the task.

questions.title: Do you already have specific people in mind?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs help generating a shortlist from scratch or is further along and comparing known candidates.

questions.title: Is this for a religious ceremony or a secular role?
questions.description: Determine whether the godparent role is tied to a baptism or christening (with faith requirements) or is purely honorary, as this defines eligibility criteria.

questions.title: Are there family expectations about who must be considered?
questions.description: Surface any cultural, traditional, or relational obligations — such as a sibling or parent expecting to be asked — that constrain the options.

questions.title: What qualities matter most to you in a godparent?
questions.description: Identify the user's top criteria — e.g., shared values, faith, proximity, life stage, reliability — to create a clear decision framework.

questions.title: What is the very next thing you need help with?
questions.description: Pin down the immediate action: brainstorming names, evaluating candidates side by side, deciding how to ask the person, or something else entirely.

questions.title: Are you worried about upsetting people who are not chosen?
questions.description: Understand whether managing the feelings of friends or family who might expect to be asked is a factor that should be built into the plan.
